0.0.n: Sets the time frame for the upcoming anniversary.

0.1.n: Marks 今週 as the topic being discussed.

0.2.n: Names the weekday of the anniversary.

0.4.n: ２月 names the second month of the year.

0.5.n: Links the month to its day; English normally puts the month first without a linking word.

0.6.n: Read はつか, a special reading for the twentieth day of a month.

1.0.n: The speaker repeats the date while organizing the sentence.

1.2.n: Read はつか; here it identifies which Thursday is meant.

1.3.n: Links the date and weekday, describing Thursday as the twentieth.

1.4.n: Names the weekday on which the anniversary falls.

1.5.n: Marks Thursday as the specific time of the anniversary.

1.6.n: Combines with たち to form 私たち, referring here to the speaker and their spouse.

1.7.n: Added to 私, this makes 私たち, meaning we.

1.8.n: Marks possession after 私たち, linking the couple to their anniversary.

1.9.n: Combines with 記念日 to name a wedding anniversary.

1.10.n: With 結婚, this refers to the yearly celebration of the couple's wedding.

1.11.n: Marks the anniversary as the thing that occurs.

1.12.n: Polite form of ある, used here for an event occurring on a particular date.

2.0.n: The speaker now explains what kind of day Thursday is.

2.1.n: Marks Thursday as the topic of the explanation.

2.2.n: Uses の to describe the following noun 日.

2.3.n: Connects 普通 to 日, forming the description ordinary day.

2.4.n: Read ひ here, unlike the special reading in the date 20日.

2.5.n: The linking form used after a noun before ので.

2.6.n: Introduces the reason they are not celebrating on Thursday.

2.8.n: Clarifies that Thursday is a regular working day rather than a day off.

2.9.n: Connects the noun 平日 to ので to give a reason.

2.10.n: Repeats the reason more specifically after the speaker clarifies 普通の日 as 平日.

3.0.n: With a negative statement, it conveys that nothing special is planned.

3.1.n: Combines with も and a negative verb to express doing nothing.

3.2.n: After 何, it works with しない to rule out any activity.

3.3.n: Plain negative form of する, referring here to their plans.

3.4.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before です.

3.5.n: Makes the explanation polite without changing the negative meaning of しない.

3.6.n: Connects this lack of Thursday plans to the alternative celebration that follows.

4.0.n: Points back to not doing anything special on Thursday.

4.1.n: Forms その代わりに, introducing an alternative to the previously mentioned plan.

4.2.n: Completes その代わりに so the phrase introduces what they will do as an alternative.

4.3.n: Names the day chosen for their celebration.

4.4.n: Links Friday to 夜, specifying which evening.

4.5.n: Refers here to the evening when they will go out for dinner.

4.6.n: Marks Friday evening as the time of their outing.

4.7.n: Directly describes レストラン without needing a linking particle.

4.8.n: A borrowed word written in katakana.

4.9.n: Marks the restaurant as the destination of 行って.

4.10.n: The て-form of 行く connects going to the restaurant with having a meal.

4.12.n: Combines with をする to express having a meal.

4.13.n: Marks 食事 as what they will do in the expression 食事をする.

4.14.n: する becomes して, followed by こよう, the intention form of 来る, suggesting an outing and return.

4.15.n: Marks the intended action as the content of 思っています.

4.16.n: 思う in the ています form expresses a current intention when paired with an intention form and と.

5.0.n: Connects this statement to the Friday dinner plan just described.

5.1.n: Names the day of the plans the speaker is anticipating.

5.2.n: Links the weekday to 夜 to specify Friday evening.

5.3.n: Refers to the time of their planned restaurant outing.

5.4.n: Marks when the speaker has plans.

5.5.n: Refers to the arranged outing, not merely an abstract intention.

5.6.n: Marks 予定 as the thing that exists in 予定がある.

5.7.n: Plain form of ある; 予定がある literally says plans exist.

5.8.n: Links having plans to the speaker's feeling of excitement.

5.10.n: Softens the degree of excitement expressed.

5.11.n: A sound-symbolic expression for happy anticipation, often used with する.

5.12.n: Polite ongoing form of する; with ワクワク, it describes the speaker's current emotional state.

0.lit: As for this week, Thursday, February's twentieth,
0.tip: 20日 is read はつか, an irregular date reading worth learning as a whole.

1.lit: The twentieth, on Thursday the twentieth, our wedding anniversary exists.
1.tip: An event があります on a date means the event occurs then.

2.lit: As for Thursday, because it is an ordinary day, because it is a weekday,
2.tip: After a noun, な connects to ので to express because it is that thing.

3.lit: We will not do anything in particular, but,
3.tip: 何も with a negative verb means not anything, or nothing.

4.lit: Instead, on Friday evening, we are thinking we will go to a nice restaurant, eat, and come back.
4.tip: An intention form followed by と思っています expresses a current plan, rather than just a passing thought.

5.lit: So, because there are plans on Friday evening, I am feeling a little excited.
5.tip: ワクワクしています describes happy anticipation of something enjoyable coming up.
